messages:
jess: FYI ACME is seeing a big p99 jump on apac realtime endpoints for small-batch traffic (batch_size 1-4). Started ~2026-02-14 01:00 UTC after infra rollout. p50 fine, p95 up a bit, p99 from ~180ms -> ~1.8s. Please triage urgently.

mike: On it. Can you paste the customer sample request + any rate info? I'm pulling traces and infra metrics now.

jess: Sample request sent to #support-attachments (curl payload). Traffic is low volume but bursty. No auth or 5xx errors, just long tails.

mike: Quick correlation: p99 aligns with spikes in host io_wait and increased KV cache miss latency on the realtime pool. Also saw higher nvme latency on some nodes.

ada: We rolled driver 535.10 -> 537.02 across apac GPU pool at 00:45 UTC and bumped kernel to 6.1.12 on the same hosts. Patch included small nvme/driver changes.

tony: Is this affecting hosted API only or dedicated as well?

jess: Hosted only (customers on shared pools). Dedicated customers not reporting issues.

mike: Repro locally against pool node (small-batch): running curl to /v1/realtime shows intermittent tail waits. Example test:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-realtime-1","inputs":["hi"],"max_tokens":16}' -w "\nTIME: %{time_total}\n"```
Many runs: time_total oscillates 0.12s -> 1.6s tail.

lee: Small-batch realtime paths rely heavily on KV cache lookups; if host IO or pagefaults increased, KV cache reads could stall GPU threads leading to token emission stalls -> tail p99.

amanda: ACME CS asked for ETA and mitigation now. Can we offer a region failover or temporary SLA workaround?

mike: Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) Route ACME traffic to eu-central fallback pool (no driver bump there). 2) Enable small-batch smoothing queue to throttle bursts. 3) Spin up fallback model variant (quantized) for ACME which reduces KV pressure. 4) Start driver rollback on affected apac nodes if infra team agrees. Which do you want first?

ada: I can open rollback window now. Before that, collecting host logs from pool-apac-1 nodes:```bash
sudo journalctl -u nvme -n 200 --no-pager
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80
```
Snippets show repeated: "nvme 0000:81:00.0: Abort command due to controller fatal error" and block_io timeouts on a subset of nodes.

mike: Check GPU runtime too:```bash
nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Driver Version' -n
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
ls -l /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
```
On repro host: Driver=537.02, CUDA=13.0. Node also shows elevated blk_io_time in iostat.

infra-bot: Rollback window created for pool-apac-1 nodes at 02:05 UTC. Automated rollback plan ready.

mike: I'll enable region failover for ACME and route traffic to eu-central. Also enabling smoothing queue for small-batch for 5m to blunt spikes. Spinning up quantized fallback now.

amanda: Communicated to ACME support: "We are routing you to eu fallback and applying mitigation; we expect p99 to drop within 10-15m."

(10m later)
mike: After failover + smoothing, ACME p99 improved to ~140ms in eu fallback. Apac pool still shows p99 ~1.6s on affected nodes.

ada: Rollback started on 6 nodes in pool-apac-1 at 02:18 UTC. Rolling driver to previous known-good 535.10.

deploy-bot: Driver rollback job started for pool-apac-1 (6 nodes). ETA ~12m.

mike: Monitoring traces — once rollback completes I'll validate tail latencies and kv cache miss latency.

(25m later)
mike: Confirmed: after driver rollback p99 returned to baseline ~110-150ms across repro tests. KV cache miss latency back to expected and host IO contention reduced.

ada: Post-rollback dmesg shows nvme errors stopped on affected nodes. We'll hold driver rollout until we reproduce and patch.

jess: ACME notified, thanks team. CS asks for postmortem and customer-grade timeline.

mike: Quick action items: - Block next apac driver rollout until root cause PR merges - Eng-infra to reproduce NVMe/controller edge-case with driver 537.02 + kernel 6.1.12 - Add automated detection: correlate driver version + host blk_io latency alert to auto-fail rollout - Update runbook to prefer region failover for small-batch p99 for hosted tenants

ada: I'll file a postmortem and link logs/rollout job.

jess: Closing customer escalation after follow-up. Will reopen if anything reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
